thread:
sam: Heads-up — EU customers hitting 500s after an edge failover around 10:11 UTC. Symptoms: requests routed to us-west, high latency, billing spike reported. Any ideas?

support-bot: Alert: EU-ingress 5xx spike 10:11–10:18 UTC. Top upstream cluster: us-west-1-a. Monitor: https://obs.example/redwood/alerts/1132 :eyes:

irene: @sam can you paste one of the raw request headers and an example curl so we can repro? Are clients sending a region hint?

sam: here's a sanitized example from a failing request:```
GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
X-Request-Id: 9f2b-...
X-Region: us-west
X-Forwarded-For: 3.121.45.67
User-Agent: curl/7.82.0

```

nate: interesting — X-Region is set to us-west in the request hitting our edge. Do we rewrite that header anywhere in the gateway chain? We recently rolled an envoy filter that preserves client-provided X-Region to support sticky routing. :thinking_face:

leo: checking envoy configs, the L7 proxy has a fallback path: when a route can't be matched it falls back to an upstream host and applies host header rewrite. I wonder if multi-hop proxies are accidentally copying the upstream's region hint into the header.

irene: steps we need: 1) confirm chain (client -> edge-gw -> internal-proxy -> inference-gw), 2) capture x-envoy-original-headers and upstream cluster chosen, 3) attempt a repro with curl that sets X-Region: eu and then force a failover.

sam: repro curl I used:```
curl -v -H "X-Region: eu" -H "Host: api.redwood.ai" "https://edge.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
I then rebooted one edge host to trigger failover and saw routing flip to us-west for ~7 minutes.

nate: I pulled a snippet from the edge logs around the failover:```
[10:11:04] edge-01 PROXY chain: src=3.121.45.67 x-region=eu -> edge-01 -> internal-proxy-07 x-region=us-west -> inference-gw-3
[10:11:06] upstream selected: cluster us-west-1-a (fallback)
[10:15:23] downstream request headers: X-Region: us-west
```
That looks like a header override happening in the proxy chain, not client-side.

leo: confirmed in the envoy config: the fallback route has an "append_x_region" behavior tied to virtual cluster runtime key. When the fallback path is taken, we call a header manipulation filter that sets X-Region from the chosen upstream cluster. There's a bug where the filter runs on the downstream path for subsequent hops and overwrites whatever was set by a previous hop.

irene: possible mitigation: strip incoming X-Region at the very edge and let internal routing set it, or roll back the header-preserve change. Which is faster?

nate: temporary mitigation I recommend: insert a filter at the edge listener to remove X-Region from client requests before any routing decisions, then let the routing layer insert the correct X-Region. Command to patch via control plane:```
PATCH /config/listener/edge-listener
Content-Type: application/json
{ "filters": [{"name":"envoy.filters.http.header_to_remove","value":"X-Region"}] }
```
Rollback plan: revert commit f2b3c that introduced "preserve-client-region" (PR #4821).

support-bot: Created support ticket S-8892, linked incident channel #incident-gw-region-flap, priority P1. Assigned: nate, leo. :rotating_light:

sam: applied the temporary strip filter at 10:34 UTC — initial telemetry shows 5xxs dropping back to baseline and EU traffic routing staying in-region. Will keep monitoring.

irene: good — Nate and Leo, please capture a minimal repro and validate the fix in staging. Also add a short postmortem draft with timeline, customer impact, and billing recommendation.

nate: repro notes I'm adding to the ticket: 1) curl with X-Region: eu, 2) induce fallback by killing edge backend (systemctl restart inference-backend), 3) observe header rewrite in internal-proxy logs. Attachments: envoy config diffs, capture commands, sample logs.

leo: root cause hypothesis for the postmortem: header-preserve filter had unintended side-effect: header rewrite on fallback path executes with the last-upstream context, causing multi-hop header bleed. Patch idea: scope header rewrite to the immediate routing decision only (do not run on downstream hop surfaces).

irene: assigning owners: eng-runtime (nate), eng-sre (leo). Support to follow up with affected customers on credits and mitigation notes.

sam: confirmed customer-facing error rates normalized by 10:46 UTC after mitigation. Will coordinate a postmortem and billing credits. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
